title: An elastic job scheduler for HPC applications on the cloud
problem: Cloud's pay-as-you-go model requires efficient resource utilization. Traditional parallel programming models (MPI) don't support autoscaling. HPC on cloud needs dynamic rescaling to match resource availability and minimize cost.
motivation: Cloud resources are elastic but HPC applications traditionally require fixed resource counts. Dynamic rescaling capability is essential for cost-effective cloud HPC. Charm++ naturally supports this; scheduler bridge needed.
method: A Kubernetes operator (automated software that manages applications) controls Charm++ parallel programs and automatically adjusts how many computing resources each gets based on what's available in the cluster. The scheduler prioritizes jobs by importance level, giving high-priority work more resources when they're scarce. As resources become available, it expands job allocations; as demand drops, it shrinks them—reducing wasted compute nodes while keeping important jobs on track.
key_novelty: The core idea is elastic, priority-aware scheduling for HPC on Kubernetes—automatically scaling job resource allocation based on cluster availability while ensuring high-priority work gets resources first.
contributions: Kubernetes operator enabling Charm++ on Kubernetes
Comparison with static schedulers showing significant improvements

metrics.cluster_utilization: Higher resource utilization vs. static scheduling

limitations: Abstract only; no specific performance numbers; unclear scalability to large clusters; Charm++ requirement limits applicability.
